claims.text: Under spec.syncPolicy.automated, Argo CD starts a sync by itself when a change in Git, such as a new commit to its folder, leaves the manifests different from the live objects; live-cluster changes do not trigger it; it tries once per commit. Without a sync policy it only compares.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: User Guide > Automated Sync Policy; deploy/gitops/lessons/staging-manual.yaml:5-6 and staging-auto.yaml:17-24 @ stage-3

claims.text: Argo CD compares the manifests from the config repository with the live objects; it does not watch a container registry for new images, so a newly pushed tag changes nothing until a manifest names it (Image Updater out of scope).
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Core Concepts / Automated Sync Policy (sync triggered by Git changes); gitops-deploy.sh:32-33 comment @ stage-3

claims.text: release.yml (on a v*.*.* git tag) builds nothing: it gives the images ci.yml pushed for the tagged commit, including donhang-api and donhang-migrate, the version (e.g. 1.0.0) as a second tag and pushes it to ghcr.io.
At stage-3 envs/staging/api.yaml (line 42) and migrate-hook.yaml (line 21) name the tag sha-bb184243e4cafed6ae833ca61710608366214aa5; a deploy changes both to the same new tag.

The Git server (gitea) runs inside the donhang-staging cluster, reached from the host only via a kubectl port-forward, so CI on GitHub's runners cannot push to it; gitops-deploy.sh commits from the host. The config repository's branch is main; the source repository's is master.
Argo CD rereads the repository on an interval; the annotation argocd.argoproj.io/refresh=normal on the Application (app_refresh) makes it compare at once. Refresh itself does not start a sync.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Operator Manual > Reconcile / FAQ (refresh vs sync, timeout.reconciliation); scripts/lib/gitops.sh:104-107 @ stage-3

claims.text: The automated sync applies the folder with its sync waves: wave 0, the migration hook in wave 1 (new migrate image), the api Deployment in wave 2; changing the Pod template image starts a rolling update whose new Pods pull 1.0.0 from ghcr.io.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Sync Phases and Waves; Kubernetes docs: Deployments > Updating a Deployment (template change triggers rollout)

claims.text: staging-auto.yaml has the same name (staging, ns argocd) as staging-manual.yaml, so applying it changes that Application, once: later deploys are only commits. Lines 3-16 match staging-manual.yaml:7-20; lines 21-24 add syncPolicy.automated, selfHeal: false, prune: false.
With selfHeal: false, automated sync does not undo changes made in the cluster; with prune: false, objects removed from Git are left running.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy (Automatic Pruning, Automatic Self-Healing); staging-auto.yaml:18-20 comment

claims.text: gitops-deploy.sh: 14 only kubectl apply (the Application); 22 perl swaps the tag in api.yaml, migrate-hook.yaml; 24 config_commit; 25 app_refresh; 26-27 wait for sync of the commit config_head --verify names; 28 rollout status; 29 Pod images counted by sort | uniq -c (the 2).
config_commit (scripts/lib/gitops.sh) commits with user.name set to the calling script's name and pushes to the Git server; git log's author column shows that name.
Git does not verify the author name of a commit: it is whatever the committer's user.name was set to (commit signing out of scope).
claims.source_hint: Git docs: git-commit (COMMIT INFORMATION, user.name / author identity) / git-config user.name

claims.text: gitops-deploy.txt: Application staging applied; 2 files changed, 2 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-); staging: Synced, Healthy; 2 api Pods on ghcr.io/duyan11110/donhang-api:1.0.0; git log newest first: gitops-deploy.sh deploy commit above gitops-repo.sh's first commit.
In the captured output, the first '...' replaces the short commit id and the second the date and time of config-repository commits, which change on every run.

With a tag that does not change (latest), pushing a new image leaves the manifest unchanged, so Argo CD stays Synced; running Pods keep their image, and a later Pod may get a different build depending on its node's cache and the pull policy (not changed to Always on an existing Deployment).
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Images > Image pull policy (default set at creation, not updated when the tag changes); Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy

claims.text: Whoever can push to envs/staging of the config repository decides what staging runs, so that repository should be protected like the cluster itself when automated sync is on.
claims.source_hint: Outline item 5; Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy

claims.text: At work, the CI job that pushed the image would commit the new tag to the config repository as its last step (when CI can reach the Git server).
